stories.title: FBI arrests OpenAI employee suspected of using a chatbot to help plant a bug in an executive meeting room
stories.summary:
The FBI has arrested an OpenAI employee suspected of planting a hidden recording device in the company's offices, allegedly with a chatbot's help.

- CNET reports US intelligence and security officials say espionage inside AI labs poses a national security threat
- Wired reports chatbot prompts reveal the engineer's alleged efforts to set up a covert listening device days before one was found in a meeting room used by top executives
- OpenAI says it asked its own AI models to work out what the device was, per Engadget
- Gizmodo notes the "sophisticated" bug appears to be a $13.99 Seeed Studio hobbyist board, and that the accused cited Elon Musk as a role model

stories.title: Microsoft's top two executives press for AI guardrails: Nadella wants an "emergency brake," its president says AI is less regulated than milk

Microsoft's two most senior executives have both publicly called for stronger AI guardrails within days of each other.

- CEO Satya Nadella wrote in a Saturday morning post that AI models need an "emergency brake," saying it is time "to step back and assess the trust architecture" of AI, TechCrunch reports

- Smith said the UK is best placed to drive AI regulation, per TechCrunch, and is calling for stronger global safety rules as AI systems grow more powerful, per Gizmodo
